prompt: Stage 3-2, level 5 with 54 gold, 76 HP. You are on a 2-cost reroll plan: your 2-cost carry is at 6 of 9 copies and you have counted 4 copies on other boards. You hold a 3-star-ready pair of 2-cost tanks too. Do you roll now at level 5 or level to 6 first?

options.label: Roll at 5 now: 2-cost odds are 33% and you need only 3 copies
Level to 6 (2 XP, one purchase), then roll to a 20-gold floor at 40% 2-cost odds
Hold and level 7 at 4-1 before rolling

explanation:
The reroll plan is not "stay low forever"; it is "roll at the level where the target cost's odds peak, and no higher". For 2-costs that is level 6: 40% per slot against 33% at 5 and only 30% at 7. You are 2 XP from 6, so the level costs a single 4-gold purchase and also gives you a sixth board slot for the bench tank pair that is about to 3-star. Rolling at 5 spends 20% worse odds on every gold, which over a 34-gold rolldown is the difference between an expected 3 copies and 2.

Contest math supports rolling now rather than at 4-1: 4 copies are already gone, 6 are yours, and a pool of 25 has 15 left; every round you wait lets the other holders take more. Level 7 at 4-1 would drop your odds and the pool would be thinner. Level 6, set a 20-gold floor, roll.
principle: A reroll plan rolls at the level where the target cost peaks, not at the lowest level you happen to be.
commonMistake: Confusing "reroll" with "never level". Skipping the 2-XP purchase costs you 7 percentage points on every shop.
